Two numbers sum to a multiple of 7 iff their residues are complementary: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), or both 0. Upper bound: from each complementary pair at most one residue class can be used entirely (mixing classes creates a bad pair), giving at most 15 + 15 + 14 = 44, plus at most one element ≡ 0 (any two multiples of 7 sum to a multiple of 7). Total ≤ 45. Construction: all n in {1..100} with n ≡ 1, 2, or 3 (mod 7) — that is {1,8,...,99} (15), {2,9,...,100} (15), {3,10,...,94} (14) — together with the single element 7. Sums of two elements from residues {1,2,3} lie in residues {2,3,4,5,6}, never 0; 7 plus any of these gives residues 1,2,3. So the set of 45 elements works and 45 is optimal.
